# Actual finite-leaf request binding

Copyright 2026 Masahiko G. Yamada. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

The finite Rust unitary adapter now reconstructs complete QIRF bytes and compares
an independent exact matrix and complete unary boundary. Its next connection
must obtain those requests from the actual pure Lean artifact, not producer
fields describing a different checked leaf.

Implement a bounded pure projection for the existing `finite` rule. Read the
actual indexed proof, definition, meaning and identity encodings. Retain the
complete leaf program and finite meaning bytes, exact input/output interface,
all four endpoint indices and the proof index. This initial adapter requires
one legacy Bit/Unit/product owner at each end, the same retained type tree,
at most six axes, a unitary equation, no premises and the ordinary version-one
empty witness. Reject malformed headers, nonidentity encodings and mismatched
endpoints; do not silently treat Bits as its finite Bit/product representation.

Prove successful projection binds every retained field to the actual arrays,
successful inspection implies the real typing/endpoint predicates and bounded
work, and a request is unique for a fixed artifact/index. Byte mutation must
change the pending request; this pass does not parse or approve opaque bytes.
Keep payload limits and the caller's remaining two-million-unit structural
allowance. The whole-artifact pass remains responsible for aggregate bytes,
reachability and one shared allowance across requests.

Native tests must distinguish `pending` from semantic acceptance, exercise
zero-width Unit owners, exact type trees, reordering actual table indices,
owner/axis/encoding mutations, six/seven-bit boundaries, and insufficient work.
Foreign payloads and phase faults can reach `pending` but must still fail the
Rust reconstruction/equation pass. No serialized success flag, foreign theorem,
new accepting derivation rule or production semantic seal is introduced.

Next integration retains explicit transitional Rust correspondence premises in
the theorem, connects these bound requests to that checker, and incorporates
their actual equations into whole-artifact derivation. This packet does not
complete those obligations or the remaining finite-effect/encoding profile.
